items.title: Trump Weighs Call for Capital Gains Tax Cuts as Midterm Boost
items.author: Josh Wingrove
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump is looking for new policy pledges he can present to voters ahead of the midterm election, according to a top economic aide and a former administration official, including potentially calling on Congress to cut capital gains taxes and create an exemption for certain home sales.</article>

items.title: CFTC Orders Kalshi to Keep Operating Despite New York Suit
items.author: Lydia Beyoud
items.content: <article>The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has ordered Kalshi to keep operating despite a legal attempt by New York’s government to shut down its operations.</article>

items.title: Markets Await CPI as AI Trade Faces Another Test | The Close 8/11/2026
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are RBC Capital Markets Head of Derivatives Strategy Amy Wu Silverman, AIG President & CEO Eric Andersen, Khosla Ventures Managing Director Keith Rabois and State Affairs CEO Evan Burns, Vertiv CEO Gio Albertazzi, SiTime Chairman & CEO Rajesh Vashist, Wells Fargo Chief Equity Strategist Ohsung Kwon, Former FDA Acting Commissioner Steve Ostroff, Upwork CEO Hayden Brown, D.A. Davidson Head of Technology Research Gil Luria, & Redpoint Ventures Managing Director Erica Brescia. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Judge Expands Block on Trump’s Mail-in Voting Plan for Midterms
items.author: Zoe Tillman
items.content: <article>A federal judge in Boston entered a nationwide order blocking the US Postal Service from carrying out President Donald Trump’s directives to overhaul mail-in voting policies before the November midterm elections, expanding an earlier halt that covered roughly half the country.</article>

items.title: Iran, US Harden Positions; eToro Crypto Revenue Misses | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/11/2026
items.content: <article>Pakistan’s defense minister said the US and Iran are “close to some sort of arrangement” over the Strait of Hormuz, even after both sides appeared to toughened their positions in the long-deadlocked negotiations. “Things are shaping up in favor of peace,” Khawaja Asif told reporters in Islamabad on Tuesday, without giving details of any breakthrough. Bloomberg News' Josh Wingrove breaks down where negotiations stand. Plus, eToro CEO Yoni Assia discusses the company's earnins report with hosts Tim Stenovec and Kristine Aquino. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Khosla Ventures' New Bet on Policy Data Company State Affairs
items.content: <article>Khosla Ventures Managing Director Keith Rabois and State Affairs CEO Evan Burns discuss why Khosla is making a new bet on State Affairs, a politics and policy data company. They speak on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Wisconsin and South Carolina Elections Test Progressives and Trump
items.author: Nancy Cook
items.content: <article>The outcomes will show the direction of both parties.</article>

items.title: Trump’s Vaccine Order Is a Nightmare
items.content: <article>Trump’s proposed sweeping changes to the childhood vaccine schedule is being pushed forward in the name of protecting parental authority. Yet it likely is making it harder for parents to protect their kids from preventable diseases, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Lisa Jarvis says. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Pakistan Says US-Iran Deal Nears | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 8/11/2026
items.content: <article>On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the primary elections in the US Tuesday. On today's show, Advancing American Freedom Chairman Marc Short, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and former Deputy United States Special Envoy to the Middle East Morgan Ortagus. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Democrats Offering Platform Voters Aren't Looking For, Says Marc Short
items.content: <article>Marc Short, chairman of Advancing American Freedom and former chief of staff to Vice President Mike Pence, said that the alternative Democrats are offering to voters tired of the Republican party is also not what Americans are looking for. Short said that Democratic Socialist candidates winning Democrat primaries gives Republicans the opportunity to craft a narrative about how 'crazy' the Democratic Party has become.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US Criticizes China Over Nuclear Missile Test in Pacific Ocean
items.author: Magdalena Del Valle and Li Liu
items.content: <article>The US criticized China for not giving sufficient notice before testing an intercontinental ballistic missile in the Pacific Ocean last month, as the Trump administration pushes back against Beijing’s growing nuclear arsenal.</article>

items.title: US Golden Dome Office Invites Industry Input Via Online Portal
items.author: Tony Capaccio
items.content: <article>The Pentagon opened an online portal for industry competitors to submit ideas and requests for information for the $185 billion Golden Dome program, in the latest effort to shake up traditional defense procurement competition.</article>

items.title: Brazil Assets Drop as Election Worries Start to Grip Traders
items.author: Gabriel Diniz Tavares, Leda Alvim and Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo
items.content: <article>Brazilian assets trailed global peers on Tuesday as political concerns start to weigh on investor sentiment two months before the presidential election.</article>

items.title: Fast-Tracked Deportations for Migrants Permitted by Court
items.author: Suzanne Monyak
items.content: <article>A federal appeals court cleared the way for the Trump administration to revive directives that put hundreds of thousands of migrants at risk to be deported under a fast-tracked process.</article>

items.title: Trump Says Russia Released Imprisoned Former Marine
items.author: Sonya Dymova
items.content: <article>US President Donald Trump said Russia had released former US Marine Robert Gilman after roughly four years.</article>

items.title: Trump’s New Birthright Citizenship Curbs Face Legal Contest
items.author: Zoe Tillman
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump’s latest move to restrict automatic citizenship is facing a legal challenge, months after the Supreme Court knocked down his earlier attempt at upending longstanding guarantees for children born in the US to non-citizens.</article>

items.title: Trump Says US Weighing Attempt to Stop NYC Pied-A-Terre Tax
items.author: Hadriana Lowenkron
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump said he would examine whether the federal government can stop New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s new pied-à-terre tax, which was temporarily blocked by a state court.</article>

items.title: Kennedy Center Must Pay Musician $250,000 in Trump Name Spat
items.author: Zoe Tillman
items.content: <article>The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington was ordered to pay more than $250,000 in legal fees to a musician who canceled a Christmas Eve concert over the venue’s move to add President Donald Trump’s name.</article>

items.title: Colombia Earthquake: Search for Survivors Underway as Death Toll Nears 170
items.author: Oscar Medina
items.content: <article>Colombia’s government plans to declare an economic emergency to bolster its response to a massive earthquake, as the country’s new president faces a tough and early test of his abilities to handle a crisis.</article>

items.title: Pakistan Says Deal Is Close Even as Iran, US Harden Stances
items.author: Josh Wingrove and Patrick Sykes
items.content: <article>Pakistan’s defense minister said the US and Iran are “close to some sort of arrangement” over the Strait of Hormuz, even after both sides appeared to toughen their positions in the long-deadlocked negotiations.</article>
